issues.claim: "One container per run. Start it in a shared fixture (for example `ICollectionFixture<T>` in xUnit)..." together with "parallel collections get separate databases in the same container"
issues.problem: An xUnit `ICollectionFixture<T>` is created once per collection, not once per run. If tests are split into several collections to run in parallel, each collection would start its own container. That contradicts "one container per run" and "separate databases in the same container". A candidate would wrongly learn that one collection fixture gives one container for the whole test run.
issues.suggestedFix: Say that one container per run needs a fixture that outlives collections: a static lazy-initialised container, or an xUnit v3 assembly fixture. Mention a per-collection fixture only for tests in a single collection, and then keep the sentence about separate databases in one shared container. Apply the same change in the RU text, for example "Контейнер - один на прогон: общий для всех коллекций (статический ленивый экземпляр или сборочная фикстура xUnit v3), а не по одному на коллекцию".

issues.claim: "Which of the three is expensive to create each time - starting the container, creating the schema, or the rows one test writes?"
issues.problem: The hint lists the three levels of the answer (container, schema, data) and asks which is expensive. This is close to giving away the answer's structure rather than nudging toward it.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a weaker nudge, for example "Which parts of the setup do all tests share, and which part can one test change without affecting the others?"

issues.claim: "Imagine you inline a helper class back into the service or put a cache in front of the repository..."
issues.problem: The hint describes the exact refactoring scenarios behind options a and b, so it is stronger than a nudge. It does not name the options, so this is only a wording issue.
issues.suggestedFix: Make it more general, for example "Pick a refactoring that keeps what the method returns and sends out unchanged. Which of these checks would still fail?"
